label: prf:qbeta-z-recursion-to-ck-recursion-bridge
title: Proof of qbeta z recursion to ck recursion bridge
html:
Algebraic rearrangement of the 3-term recursion 4(n+1) · a_{n+1} + 6n · a_n + (2n-1) · a_{n-1} = 0 from Per-block character closed forms for \chi_\lambda(\Delta_{T_\beta})(q) over H_3(q) §Extension #5, dividing through by 4(n+1) (positive for n \geq 0). \square

Structural relationship to the constant-kernel recursion

The constant-kernel recursion defined in c_k precision-ladder recursion induced by the fibre-level Habiro q-difference equation captures the constant-kernel depth-d linear recursion

  c_{k+1} = \sum_{j=0}^{d-1} \text{kernel}(j) \cdot c_{k-j}

where (\text{kernel}(j))_{0 \le j < d} is a fixed coefficient vector independent of k. The z-Taylor recursion above also has depth 2 in the sense that each step uses two prior coefficients (a_n and a_{n-1}), but its kernel coefficients depend on n:

Property constant-kernel recursion z-Taylor recursion
Depth d (fixed) 2
Kernel R^d (constant) n \mapsto (\text{Fin 2} \to \mathbb{R}) (variable)
Linear in history Yes (proven) Yes (state-dependent linear)

Origin of the kernel difference. The constant kernel of the ladder recursion reflects a fibre-level Habiro element whose q-difference equation F(q \xi) = R(q, \xi) \cdot F(\xi) has a Laurent polynomial R of fixed degree d; the change-of-basis from the Habiro (u; u)_m ring to the ladder u^k inherits the constant kernel. The z-Taylor recursion, by contrast, is the descent of a second-order linear ODE with rational coefficients for z(q) = \sqrt q / (1 + q) around q = 1; the ODE's polynomial-in-q coefficients become polynomial-in-n recursion coefficients under Taylor expansion.

Bridge to closure. A constant-kernel recursion for the c_k cannot be obtained from the z-Taylor recursion alone (the kernel shapes differ). However:

  1. The Q_\beta ladder c_k — which the constant-kernel recursion ultimately describes — is conjectured to be expressible in the z-basis via the open f-map. If the f-map identifies the Habiro element F(q) whose Taylor coefficients are the c_k, and if F(q)'s q-difference equation has constant Laurent coefficients in \xi, then the resulting constant-kernel recursion would inherit its kernel from F — not from the z-recursion.
  2. The z-recursion's role in this picture is upstream auxiliary data: the Markov parameter z(q) enters \Delta\mathrm{tr}_M(q) through the canonical Wenzl weights y_\lambda(q) (see Per-block character closed forms for \chi_\lambda(\Delta_{T_\beta})(q) over H_3(q) §Extension #4), and the z-Taylor expansion is what one would eventually convolve against the per-block characters to recover the f-map. The z-recursion is a structural input to the f-map derivation, not a substitute for the ladder c_k recursion.

Claims not established here

  • A concrete constant-kernel recursion for the c_k. That would require the open f-map identification.
  • A formula for the c_k in terms of the a_n. Open, contingent on the f-map.
